currentContext.business: Maral Overseas Limited is an integrated textile company with capabilities across yarns, fabrics and garments, headquartered in Noida and serving leading corporates and brands across India and international markets. Its yarn and fabric manufacturing operations are centred at the Maral Sarovar facility in one of India's key cotton growing regions, while garmenting operations are based in the NCR region. The yarn division is described as the flagship business providing scale, flexibility and product depth across cotton, blended and specialised yarns; the fabric and garment divisions are the stated focus for scaling value creation and deepening partnerships with global brands.

currentContext.expansion: FY2026 was a year in which Maral's headline rupee capex plan was SHELVED while smaller, self-funded capacity work went ahead. The Directors' Report (item 3, 'Modernization, Expansion and Diversification') records that the Rs 30.66 Crore capital expenditure plan for modernization, replacement of machinery and capacity additions in Yarn Dyeing and the fabric Dye house at the Sarovar plant - a plan carried over from the previous year's report - 'has been kept in abeyance due to financial constraints'. In its place, 'certain critical machinery for improvement in efficiency in production of Fabric and Yarn division were taken on long term lease for smooth operations of the Plant without disruption in production', i.e. capacity access was rented rather than bought. Against that, three concrete capacity actions ARE claimed. (1) Dyed yarn: the Corporate Overview Yarn Division states consistent order flows were 'further reinforced by a 25% capacity expansion in dyed yarn' - a percentage step-up with no stated absolute before/after level and no stated commissioning date. (2) Melange: 'the Melange Unit progressively scaled up operations, reaching full capacity and achieving its highest production levels', described as 'well-positioned to become a key driver of growth and profitability for the yarn business in the years ahead'; the MD&A independently calls the scaling of melange yarn production to full capacity 'a significant achievement during the year'. (3) Fabric: 'Capacity within the fabric division was enhanced through targeted de-bottlenecking measures between dyed and white fabric operations, enabling better production balancing, improved throughput, and greater operational flexibility'. Forward intent is stated twice in near-identical language in the Yarn and Fabric divisional outlooks: 'A key focus area is capacity expansion, which is expected to enhance production capabilities and enable the Company to meet rising market demand in the coming years effectively' and 'A key priority is capacity expansion, which is expected to enhance production capabilities, improve operational efficiencies, and support rising business volumes in the years ahead' - neither carries a project name, a quantum or a date. The Directors' Report adds that 'capacity augmentation initiatives undertaken during the year are expected to support higher value-added production and improve operational flexibility going forward'. Client-side expansion is also stated: in alignment with the anticipated India-EU and India-UK Free Trade Agreements the Company 'is also actively expanding its client base, with a particular emphasis on markets in Europe and the United Kingdom', and is 'actively reducing its dependence on concentrated geographies and exploring opportunities across other FTA-led nations'. On energy assets, the Company 'has substantially replaced coal with biomass as its primary energy source' (Corporate Overview Fabric Division outlook, risks_esg bundle). UTILISATION AND OUTPUT, which are NOT capacity: company-wide 'Total Capacity Utilisation' is printed as 71.28% in the Corporate Overview 'Key Business Statistics'; the Fabric Division snapshot prints 58.21% and the Garment Division snapshot 66.94%, both labelled 'Total Capacity Utilisation' for FY2026. Divisional output charts print Yarn Division production of 22,054.23 tonnes and sales of 15,344.25 tonnes in FY2026, and Fabric Division production of 8,816.28 tonnes; the Garment snapshot prints production of 33,17,576 pcs. The Directors' Report separately records FY2026 production of 16,160 MT of grey yarn (FY25 16,337 MT), 3,087 MT of dyed yarn (FY25 3,183 MT), 3,477 MT of grey knitted fabric (FY25 4,026 MT), 5,339 MT of processed fabric (FY25 5,879 MT), 2,807 MT of melange yarn (FY25 2,510 MT) and 33.18 Lakh pieces of garments (FY25 44.12 Lakh pieces). Every one of these is production or utilisation, not installed capacity, and is excluded from installed_capacity by rule. CAPACITY GAP: no spindle or rotor count appears anywhere in the six routed bundles. The Yarn Division 'Performance Snapshot' box - the sibling of the Fabric and Garment snapshot boxes that carry machine counts - falls in a truncation gap between the profile bundle (which cuts off mid-word at 'strengthe') and this bundle (which resumes after it). Spinning capacity is therefore unavailable, not absent from the report.

risks.risk: US tariff escalation and trade-policy uncertainty
risks.note: The only item the MD&A explicitly types as 'Risk' in its 'Global Economic Trends and Maral Overseas' table: 'US tariff escalation; financial market volatility ... This could have an impact on the Company's market capitalisation.' The Indian-economy narrative names 'the 50% tariff imposed by the United States on selected Indian goods in August 2025'. It bites at the operating level too: grey yarn suffered 'subdued demand and pricing challenges ... particularly from domestic exporters catering to the US market, resulting in adverse demand and supply equilibrium'; the garment 'business environment remained soft, particularly in the US market due to tariff uncertainties'; and in fabric, demand was weak 'along with shifting of garment sourcing to lower tariff regions'. The MD&A SWOT lists 'Uncertainty in international trade policies, tariffs, and regulatory barriers' as a Threat.

risks.risk: Raw material price volatility, principally cotton
risks.note: Named as a Weakness in the MD&A SWOT - 'Volatility in raw material prices impacts cost structures and profitability' - and repeated as a Challenge in both divisional tables: 'Fluctuations in cotton and other fibre prices directly impact cost structures and margins' (Yarn) and 'Volatility in input prices significantly influences overall cost structures and impacts margin stability in fabric manufacturing' (Fabric). The sector narrative adds that margin pressure came from 'Volatility in raw material prices - particularly cotton - alongside elevated logistics and energy costs'. Structural for a spinner: the fabric division states it uses 'premium imported cotton'.

risks.risk: Fragmented industry structure and lack of pricing power
risks.note: MD&A SWOT Weakness: 'Intense competitive pressures arising from a highly fragmented industry structure.' Both divisional challenge tables restate it as a margin mechanism - 'Intense competition across domestic and global yarn markets continues to limit pricing power and compress margins' and 'Intense competition across domestic and global fabric markets continues to restrict pricing power and exert pressure on margins'. The garment narrative shows the mechanism in action: the tariff-driven redirection to Europe 'intensified competition and exerted pricing pressure within the EU'.

A structural concentration the report discloses without labelling it a risk: exports (FOB) accounted for 47.91% of turnover in FY2026 against 44.35% in FY2025 - i.e. the export dependence rose in the year tariffs escalated (Directors' Report, back-filled from the same bundle's Operational Performance section). The fabric division separately states exports contribute nearly 49.71% of divisional revenue, across East Asia, the Americas, the Middle East and Africa. Management is explicit that the concentration is being unwound: 'Maral is actively reducing its dependence on concentrated geographies and exploring opportunities across other FTA-led nations to build a more diversified and resilient revenue mix', with the trigger being 'Political instability in Bangladesh, coupled with the recent United States-Bangladesh Zero Tariff Trade Understanding'.

risks.risk: Demand cyclicality tied to global retail and fashion cycles
risks.note: Listed as a Challenge in both divisional tables: 'Reliance on global retail and fashion cycles leads to demand volatility, resulting in order fluctuation and inventory imbalances' (Yarn) and 'Dependence on global retail and fashion cycles introduces variability in demand, often leading to fluctuations in order volumes and imbalances in inventory levels' (Fabric). Corroborated by the dyed-yarn observation of 'shorter booking cycles', i.e. reduced forward visibility, and by weak Western consumer spending: 'macroeconomic headwinds in key Western markets, particularly the United States and the European Union ... weighed on consumer spending, which in turn affected apparel offtake'.

risks.risk: Supply chain and geopolitical disruption affecting fibre availability and delivery
risks.note: Yarn Challenge: 'Geopolitical uncertainties and logistics constraints may impact fibre availability, production cycles, and timely deliveries.' Fabric Challenge: 'Geopolitical disruptions and supply chain bottlenecks affect raw material availability, disrupt manufacturing schedules, and challenge the timely delivery of finished fabrics.' The MD&A macro section names the specific vector - 'escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, particularly the Iran-Israel/US conflict and disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz' - and the SWOT Threat 'Rising global instability and protectionist sentiment'.

risks.risk: Financial constraint limiting reinvestment, with a cumulative preference claim accruing ahead of equity
risks.note: Structural rather than cyclical, and the report states it plainly: the Rs 30.66 Crore Sarovar modernization capex was 'kept in abeyance due to financial constraints', with critical machinery taken on long-term lease instead; no equity dividend was recommended 'in view of the current financial position of the Company'; the 9.25% RNCPS dividend could not be paid because 'profits of the Company for the financial year 2025-26 are not adequate', so it accrues cumulatively and becomes payable only when the Company has sufficient profits; and the Company had no statutory CSR obligation for FY2026 because of 'losses incurred in preceding three (3) financial years'. Back-filled with provenance from Directors' Report items 3, 6 and 7, which sit in the strategy_outlook and capex_expansion bundles - the risks_esg bundle truncates at item 6. It sits in direct tension with management's stated priority that 'A key priority is capacity expansion'.

risks.risk: Continuous reinvestment required to hold technological and sustainability standing
risks.note: Both divisional challenge tables make this an explicit, recurring capital demand: 'Rapid advancements in spinning technologies and evolving sustainability standards necessitate ongoing investments to remain competitive deliver high-quality, and future-ready yarns' (Yarn) and 'Ongoing advancements in manufacturing technologies and evolving sustainability benchmarks require continuous investment to sustain competitiveness, enhance quality, and deliver future-ready fabric solutions' (Fabric). Material because the same report records discretionary capex being deferred for financial reasons.
